transcript: if Taylor Swift albums were Sondheim musicals here's what I think they'd be for Debut I'm going with Saturday Night one of Sondheim's very earliest works it feels extremely youthful both in the writing and the subject matter of young love, coming of age etc for Fearless I'm going with West Story Story which is also very much about young love very romantic at times but with a bit more bite and maturity to it and of course they both have Romeo & Juliet connections I struggled a little bit with Speak Now but I ended up going with Assasslns because in very different ways I think they're both about people who are desperate to be heard and to prove themselves for Red I have to go with Passion which is about how in a love affair passionate romance and toxicity can blur together in confusing ways for 1989 I went with Merrily we roll along and I think both of these are kind of fatalistic in the way that they portray a relationship that was maybe doomed to fail also, I hate to say it but this might have been Taylor Swift in her most Franklin Shepherd era for Reputation I picked Sweeney Todd you've got this protagonist who feels scorned by the world and puts on this persona that is hard and vengeful but underneath it's really all about love Lover was kind of a no brainer for me, I picked Company about a person who reaches a point in their life where they're looking around and sorting out what is important to them particularly confronting what it means to be in a long term committed relationship for Folklore, I went with into the Woods which like yes there's the obvious woodsy fairytale aesthetic but even beyond that I think it's more how they're both using stories fiction to explore very personal relatable themes the loss of innocence and things in reality maybe not being as they seem okay evermore is one that I really struggled with and I ended up landing on Here We Are they are very different in tone and Here We Are centers around this satirical commentary of modern society whereas evermore is definitely more personal but they're both kind of experimental and embrace a sense of dreamlike chaos and I think the central premise of Here We Are where these characters are totally adrift and then totally stuck does resonate with the feeling of evermore for Midnights I picked Follies and you would think with this aesthetic that I would save it for Life of a Showgirl but when I looked at it thematically I couldn't quite justify it Follies struck me as a much better fit for Midnights in the sense that it deals with looking back on the past with both fondness and regret the roads you didn't take etc all while this long term relationship is on the brink of collapse for Tortured Poets, I went with Sunday in the park with George and I think there's actually a lot here superficially of course you have the tortured artist both of them wrestle with public judgement public scrutiny even when it comes to the relationship dynamics they don't mirror each other one to one exactly but there's a lot of thematic commonality Stability vs. romance lack of emotional availability the feeling of being iced out but for Life of a Showgirl, I went with a Little Night Music which is also about the life of a showgirl, by the way “Heigh ho the glamorous life” anyone? before I said I couldn't quite justify picking Follies for this one a Little Night Music is considerably more joyful and romantic but there is also some drama and some sadness in the mix so let me know how you think I did does this feel right to you? or would you pick other ones?
